newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA MINERS UNIONS PROTEST OVER LEADER'S ARREST.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA MINERS UNIONS PROTEST OVER LEADER'S ARREST.

text.p: Leaders of Romania's Jiu Valley coalminers on Saturday protested against the detention of their boss, accused of spearheading bloody coalminer riots which toppled the first post-communist government in 1991.
State news agency Rompres said coalminers union leaders met in their Western stronghold of Petrosani to denounce the arrest their vigilante boss, Miron Cosma.
Police detained Cosma on Friday on a 30-day warrant issued by prosecutors over "undermining state authority" and breaking firearms regulations, charges which carry up to 15 years jail.

The move has sparked mixed reactions in the impoverished Balkan country, where the new centrist government has pledged tough reforms, including recent fuel price rises which have triggered a wave of price hikes.
In an statement issued from their Petrosani headquarters on Saturday, miners leaders said they declined "responsibility for any unrest" that might follow Cosma's arrest.
But police said spirits were calm in Petrosani, the main Jiu Valley mining town, 350 km (218 miles) west of Bucharest.
Centrist president Emil Constantinescu has accepted a request from Jiu Valley miners leaders to meet him at his Cotroceni palace on Sunday, a presidential official said.

Cosma led thousands of Jiu Valley coalminers on a three-day rampage to Bucharest in 1991, when government offices were torched and three people were killed during clashes with security forces. A date for his trial has yet to be set.
Former reformist Prime Minister Petre Roman hailed Cosma's arrest, saying it was "high time for justice have its say."
Roman, head of parliament's upper Senate, was ousted during anti-reform riots in 1991, which he later blamed on a putsch engineered by communists around ex-president Ion Iliescu.

Romania's new centrist ruling coalition has pledged to bring to justice those responsible for political violence in early post-communist years when Cosma's miners ransacked opposition party offices and beat up anti-Iliescu protesters.

Iliescu called Cosma's arrest an "exaggerated move", saying that the 1991 riots had been "spontaneous." He has repeatedly denied accusations of resorting to mob rule, by summoning the miners to the capital to crush opposition protests.
Cosma's star has been on the wane in recent years, when the former vigilante leader turned into a well-dressed labour boss.
His bid for a parliament seat was thwarted in general and presidential elections last November, when Iliescu's leftists were thrown out of office for the first time in seven years.
